pageCache.pageTitle: Home - Boarding School for Girls in Sussex | Mayfield
pageCache.text:
Mayfield is a leading independent day and boarding school providing an enriched, diverse and dynamic education for girls aged 11-18. Here, students are encouraged to chart ambitious courses, make bold decisions, and uncover their unique passions and capabilities.
Meeting the needs of the age
While academic excellence is fundamental to everything we do, what truly sets us apart is our commitment to intellectual, philosophical, and personal growth. Our girls are encouraged to embark on a Mayfield adventure that will shape their lives for years to come.
Academic excellence with heart
Our rounded approach nurtures intellectual curiosity alongside emotional resilience, producing outstanding results while developing the whole person.
Explore our curriculum
Beyond the classroom
Our vibrant programme of 80+ extracurricular activities builds confidence, teamwork and leadership skills that prepare students for future success.
Nurturing body, mind and spirit
Our Catholic ethos and Cornelian values encourage Mayfield girls to think deeply about their place in the world, developing strong moral frameworks while respecting diverse perspectives. Read about our ethos
The school feels like a joyful retreat, but there’s nothing sleepy about it. Confident in its identity, it mindfully gets on with educating girls to a high academic standard while nurturing compassion and empathy. - Good Schools Guide
A supportive community
Our diverse community of students from more than 20 nationalities creates a rich environment where every girl is valued and supported.
Learn about pastoral care
Flexible boarding options
Whether you need flexi or full boarding, we offer various options to suit your circumstances, with comfortable accommodation and dedicated House staff.
Explore boarding life
The Mayfield girl
Our students leave with more than impressive academic results! They leave with a strong sense of self, a moral compass, and the confidence to navigate an ever-changing world. Read our latest news
Every pupil is seen and understood - ISI Inspection March 2026
80% A*-B Grades at A Level
A Significant Strength in preparing girls for adult life
Girls get ‘hands on’ with emerging technologies
Our Ceramics Studio is among the best in Europe
Built on the principles of trust, respect and support for each member of the community
Winning more national titles than any other school
Class of 1987 Fenella is an award-winning actor and artist. She trained at RADA and has worked across film, television, radio, and theatre. She starred in Bright Young Things and won Sunday Times Stage Performance of the Year for her portrayal of Margaret Thatcher in Handbagged. A regular on BBC Radio 4, she has also appeared on the BBC, ITV, and international networks. In 2019, she won Sky Arts Celebrity Portrait Artist of the Year.
Class of 2011 Emily is an Olympic Champion, winning a gold medal in the Women’s Lightweight Double Sculls at the Paris 2024 Olympics alongside her rowing partner, Imogen Grant. We were thrilled to welcome Emily back to school to officially open our new Wellbeing Centre in September 2024.
Class of 1992 Camilla is an award-winning Sculptor, specialising in wildlife. Her work has been exhibited by established galleries since 2000 and bought by private collectors worldwide. She has won awards from the British Sporting Art Trust, the Society of Wildlife Artists and was recently shortlisted for the David Shepherd Wildlife Artist of the Year.
Class of 1981 Giovanna is a Medtech entrepreneur who co-founded Forte Medical with her brother Dr Vincent Forte, retired NHS GP. Their ambition was to bring Vincent’s innovation Peezy Midstream to clinical settings the world over, transforming an overlooked but common routine diagnostic process whilst improving infection control, patient safety and introducing cost-savings. All of this whilst helping to fight the growing crisis of antimicrobial resistance (AMR).
Class of 1983 Catherine is a science writer specialising in medical research, science, and nature. After earning a PhD in Immunology, she moved from research to writing and has authored books including Meet Your Bacteria and 10 Women Who Changed Science and the World. At Mayfield, she studied Maths, Biology, and Chemistry at A Level. She fondly remembers lifelong friendships and singing in Schola, a passion she continues today.
Class of 2000 Harriet is a journalist and broadcaster, specialising in female leadership. Harriet founded and edited the Guardian's Women in Leadership section, which focuses on women in the workplace, and now writes for them on Women in Tech. She is also a columnist for Psychologies magazine and hosts The Badass Women's Hour on TalkRadio. She has also written for publications including The Times, Huffington Post, and The Pool.
Class of 2018 Chelsea is currently in her second year of foundation training with the NHS, working at King’s College London and based at the Princess Royal University Hospital. She is especially interested in Paediatrics after a NICU placement but is exploring other specialities. At Mayfield, she studied Biology, Chemistry, Maths, and Latin at A Level. As Head Girl, she mentored younger students, played sports, sang in Schola Cantorum, and served at Mass. She loved the variety of opportunities at Mayfield, with a highlight being her lead role in Animal Farm, which boosted her confidence in public speaking and performance.

pageCache.pageTitle: Drama Department - Catholic School For Girls | Mayfield
pageCache.text:
Drama Department
The Drama Department offers a warmly welcoming atmosphere, where students can develop their artistic, communication and organisational skills. Opportunities in lighting, sound, make-up, costume and acting, ensure there are plenty of opportunities for each girl to find her role and her strengths. Drama education is the acquisition of transferable skills and techniques necessary for performing to an audience. It promotes the emotional development of our girls, boosting their confidence. It is also a means of exploring the world in which we live in a safe environment.
In Years 7 to 9, pupils study one period of Drama per week, covering a variety of themes ranging from basic skills, Greek Theatre, Melodrama, Shakespeare, Devised Drama and script exploration. Their learning builds towards the GCSE Drama course which engages and encourages the girls to reach their full potential as performers and theatre-makers. They learn to collaborate with others, think analytically and evaluate effectively. This leads onto A Level Drama and Theatre. Students regularly attend professional theatre productions and are encouraged to attend organised workshops. Higher education institutions value the skills that these courses offer, and students who have studied with us have gone on to study Drama at both high-ranking universities and esteemed Drama Schools. Drama also lends itself to other undergraduate degrees: we have seen girls study a diverse range of subjects, from Anthropology to Business.
Co-curricular Drama plays a big part in the life of Mayfield girls and we offer a range of activities and opportunities for all ages and abilities. Our whole whole musical is performed annually at Trinity Theatre in Tunbridge Wells, giving girls from years 7-13 to collaborate on a large-scale spectacular. Girls can opt into performing (acting/singing/dancing), playing in the orchestra or supporting the production technically (set/ stage management/ lighting/ sound/ costume/ props/ hair/ make-up). Mayfield Theatre Company is open to Years 7 to 10 and runs from February-June, culminating in a Summer production which is performed in our Concert Hall. Our annual Inter-House Drama event gives an air of competition to the art. From a set theme, each house is expected to create, direct and perform a piece of drama, which is judged by an external judicator. Individual and shared Speech and Drama lessons are popular, preparing girls for LAMDA examinations. Professional productions, practitioner workshops and creative speakers are frequent visitors to the Department.
The Drama Department consists of four drama specialist practitioners: After gaining a BA (Hons) in Drama at Bristol University, Ms Victoria Nash, Director of Drama, then gained a PGCE (Secondary) Drama at Middlesex University. She subsequently led Drama in a range of schools, before joining Mayfield in 2023. She combines her career with raising her three children, vegetarian cookery and yoga. Mr Daniel Smith has been involved in theatre from a young age, performing and directing extensively before completing his degree and PGCE in Drama. Mr Smith also continues to practice his craft, which serves to ultimately enrich the students. LAMDA teacher Jen Junemann trained at the Bristol Old Vic Theatre School, and has been working as a professional actor for over a decade. Her credits range from Shakespeare to Sondheim and she has toured the UK and the world honing her craft. A passionate feminist, Jen served 6 years as Vice Chair of the Equity Women’s Committee, working to improve working conditions for female identifying workers. Jen loves teaching LAMDA at Mayfield, where her results are consistently outstanding, with a yearly average of 95% of her students receiving a Distinction. In addition, three of her Mayfield students have successfully gained places in the National Youth Theatre. Jen continues to divide her time between professional acting, teaching and parenting.
LAMDA teacher Donna Canale trained at Guildhall School of Music and Drama, and has been working as a professional actor, singer/songwriter and session jazz vocalist for many years. She has taught LAMDA in schools for over thirteen years and believes that imagination is one of the key ingredients in a well-rounded student and that LAMDA lessons add value to every student by guiding them in a way where they can think about events and characters outside their own experience. She currently volunteers as musical director within her community choir and runs Jazz Singing classes for adults.

pageCache.pageTitle: Biology - Girls Independent School | Mayfield School
pageCache.text:
Biology
Biology is taught within a combined science curriculum in Year 7 and by subject specialists from Years 8 to 13. Biology comprises a broad range of disciplines encompassing the study of life from the molecular level, through cells, tissues and organisms, to populations and ecosystems. Advances in biological sciences have direct relevance to our everyday lives: for example, new medical treatments, especially technological advances in genetics, cancer diagnosis and treatment, the protection of endangered species, and the development of new food products. These breakthroughs have improved the quality of life for millions of people, led to a greater understanding of our impact on the environment, and the need for better resource management and conservation. Biology is of interest to anyone wanting to understand more about the way these issues will affect their lives.
GCSE
Girls follow AQA Biology, Chemistry and Physics, as separate subjects, and a small group as part of a Combined Science ‘trilogy’ course. This ensures that every pupil studies a balanced science curriculum. The curriculum tests knowledge and understanding of Biology and the application, analysis and evaluation of that knowledge in a context relevant to the 21st century. It is designed to develop core skills for studying Biology at A Level.
A Level
Girls follow the AQA A level Biology course. They learn about many aspects of biological sciences in an interesting, informative and intellectually stimulating way. This builds on the knowledge gained at GCSE and covers topics as diverse as cancer treatment with epigenetic therapy, to the impact of intensive farming on the environment. Our experienced teachers work to ensure that every individual girl has the very best opportunity to achieve her full potential through guided and independent learning. Science is taught in purpose built, subject specific laboratories supported by a team of three science technicians.As a result of studying Biology at Mayfield, girls have recently gone on to study Medicine at a wide variety of universities from Bristol to Southampton; Midwifery at Leeds University, and Veterinary Medicine at Edinburgh, as well as a range of other courses including Biochemistry, Biological and Medicinal Chemistry, and Environmental Sciences. Girls in Year 7 and 8 have the opportunity to join Lower School Science Club, as well as attending a variety of lectures and careers events by external speakers and returning pupils. In addition, girls in Year 9 attend a summer STEM careers fair. In KS4, all Year 10 girls participate in the Biology Challenge, an online competition run by the Society of Biology. We also run Dissection Club for pupils in Years 11 to 13 to research the anatomy of a wide variety of living organisms. A Level students also participate in online competitions run by The Society of Biology and attend lectures by prominent scientists in London.
Laura Lewis joined Mayfield as Head of Biology in September 2023. Educated locally in Tunbridge Wells she then studied at the University of Leeds achieving a BSc in Biochemistry and Genetics followed by a Post Graduate Diploma in Law in London. After a short stint working in the City she completed her PGCE at the University of Greenwich in 2010. Prior to joining Mayfield she worked as Biology teacher at Kent College Pembury for 13 years, during this time she held several additional roles including Assistant Head of Lower School and Head of Year. She has extensive experience as a senior A-Level Biology examiner and marks multiple papers each year. She very much enjoys using this experience to help pupils achieve the best possible outcomes. She leads a very strong team of 4 experienced biologists who aim to inspire pupils to develop a love of Biology and a realisation of the importance of science in their world, through a variety of learning opportunities and extra-curricular activities. Laura lives minutes from Mayfield and very much enjoys being able to work within her local community. She is kept busy with a young family and spends a lot of time with their horses. She has been delighted to combine her equine and biology passions by teaching the science aspects of the BTech Equine Management course.

pageCache.pageTitle: Chemistry - Girls Independent School | Mayfield School
pageCache.text:
Chemistry
Chemistry is taught within a rotation of the three sciences in Year 7 and Year 8 and by subject specialists from Years 9 to 13. GCSE pathways are chosen and begun in Year 10. Chemistry maintains its important position in school curricula as it is the science of the molecular scale, and it is at the molecular level that major advancements are being made in areas such as medicine, nanotechnology, new materials, and the environment. It follows that a firm understanding of Chemistry is required in order to participate in these exciting developments.
GCSE
Almost all girls follow either the single Chemistry or Trilogy (combined sciences) programmes from the AQA, with some Mayfield embellishments designed to ensure that the girls find the subject interesting and motivating. On completion of these pathways the girls will have been prepared for further study at A level of this or other closely related subjects, should they so choose. Learning objectives centre on introductions to atomic structure, reactivity, bonding and substance property, in both inorganic and organic worlds, often explored through experimentation. The mole concept and the calculation of ‘how much’ is contrasted with ‘how fast’ before these ideas are applied to everyday contexts, environmental issues, and interesting industrial processes, old and new.
A Level
At A Level, the Department has chosen the OCR Chemistry A specification because of the experimental and problem-solving approach it facilitates. The greater level of detail and depth of knowledge at this stage reveals the sub-divisions of the subject in to physical, organic and inorganic domains, each with its own emphasis on particular types of content and interpretative skills. It is the acquisition of technical, analytical, numerical and critical thinking skills that is so highly valued, and leads to Chemistry A Level students being sought after by Russell Group universities, high status degree courses and a wide variety of careers. Chemistry is taught in purpose built, subject specific laboratories with interactive white boards, supported by a specialist technician. Science clubs and clinics are available to all pupils across the Years 7-11 while Sixth Form chemists can work towards and take part in the elite Chemistry Olympiad competition, or carry out independent research within the British Science Association CREST Gold award framework.

Computer Science
In an era where technology intertwines with every aspect of our lives, our Computer Science curriculum equips our students to meet the needs of the age. At Mayfield School, we recognize the paramount importance of not only understanding technology but mastering its creation and contemplating its societal impact. Our curriculum is meticulously crafted to intertwine with the ever-evolving digital landscape, offering students an in-depth insight into how technology is shaping our world. Our curriculum revolves around the belief that technology is an empowering tool. This philosophy steers our lessons towards a holistic approach that transcends traditional technical skills. Students delve into the realms of coding, data privacy, cybersecurity, computer systems and artificial intelligence, gaining a comprehensive understanding of these pivotal areas. The curriculum is more than just about learning to code; it’s about creating responsible digital citizens who comprehend the ethical and societal implications of technology. Our approach is hands-on and minds-on. Students engage in compelling projects, such as building and programming robots, employing machine learning, and tackling real-world challenges. These practical applications of computer science principles, from robotics to artificial intelligence, are not only academically stimulating but also incredibly fun and rewarding. Participation in competitions like Pi Wars, the British Informatics Olympiad, CyberFirst for girls, and Lockheed Martin Code Quest is a testament to our commitment to excellence. These platforms provide our students with invaluable opportunities to showcase their skills, collaborate, and compete at a national level, further enhancing their learning experience.
Mr Stevie Partington is the Director of IT at Mayfield School. Educated at the University of Sheffield, Stevie studied for a BMus degree where he crafted Sonic Art and software tools for sound editing through computer code. Practical applications of Computer Science have always been a passion which are evident through his work in theatrical and entertainment lighting and video production as well as more out-of-this-world hobbies such as high-altitude ballooning. In his spare time, Stevie enjoys mountain walking and biking with his wife and labrador.

English
Read. Create. Think. Perform.
English teaches you to understand the world and communicate with confidence, creativity and purpose. At Mayfield, English is a vibrant and enriching subject that develops intellectual curiosity, empathy and critical thinking through the study of literature, language and performance.
Whether analysing Shakespeare, crafting original poetry, debating ideas or performing dramatic extracts, students are encouraged to discover their own voice while engaging with some of the most powerful writing ever created.
The Curriculum
From Year 7 onwards, students explore a rich and varied curriculum that includes poetry, drama, fiction and non-fiction. Alongside studying great writers from across the centuries, students develop their own skills as writers, speakers and performers.
Reading lies at the heart of everything we do. Through independent reading, students expand their vocabulary, deepen their understanding of the world and develop empathy and imagination.
Read poetry, plays and novels every year
Write their own fiction and poetry
Develop persuasive and discursive writing skills
Build confidence through speaking and performance
IGCSE & A Level
All students study both IGCSE English Language and IGCSE English Literature, providing a strong foundation in communication, analysis and critical thinking.
At A Level, students have the opportunity to study English Literature in greater depth, engaging with an even wider range of texts and developing sophisticated analytical and interpretative skills.
A mixture of introspection and passion with a touch of logic that fascinates me endlessly." Former Mayfield student
Beyond the Classroom
English at Mayfield extends far beyond lessons. We offer a rich programme of competitions, performances and literary events that encourage students to challenge themselves creatively and intellectually.
These events inspire students of all ages to develop confidence, creativity and a lifelong appreciation of literature.

pageCache.pageTitle: Art - Boarding School in Sussex | Mayfield School
pageCache.text:
Art
Creativity Without Limits
Art at Mayfield encourages students to question, experiment and express their ideas with confidence. Through drawing, painting, photography, textiles, sculpture and mixed media, students develop technical skill, creative independence and a deeper understanding of the visual world around them.
Working in a stimulating studio environment, students are encouraged to be adventurous and ambitious in their creative practice, developing the confidence to take risks, solve problems and communicate their ideas in original and personal ways.
The Curriculum
From Year 7 through to A Level, students are encouraged to develop their own creative strengths while building a strong foundation in artistic skills and processes. Art is taught through practical exploration, experimentation and critical study of artists and designers. Drawing and painting underpin much of the creative process, while students also work across a wide range of media and techniques.
At GCSE and A Level, students follow the Art and Design course and can explore areas including:
Drawing and Painting
Sculpture and Three-Dimensional Form
Photography and Digital Manipulation
Printmaking and Mixed Media
The department comprises three specialist studios, a photography studio, darkroom facilities and dedicated Sixth Form working spaces, enabling students to work across both traditional and contemporary disciplines.
Beyond the Classroom
Creativity extends well beyond timetabled lessons. Students are encouraged to develop their practice through additional workshops, independent projects and opportunities to explore new techniques and materials.
Regular workshops offer experiences in areas such as:
Photography and Photoshop
These sessions allow students to refine their skills, experiment with new approaches and develop their individual artistic style.
Degree Courses
Many students continue their creative journey at university, studying disciplines such as:
Foundation Art and Design
Recent destinations include leading institutions such as Central Saint Martins, Kingston University, UCL, Ravensbourne, Leeds, Edinburgh and Oxford Brookes.
Recent trips
Artist talks and workshops
Exhibitions and cultural events
Experiencing original artwork firsthand allows students to develop a deeper understanding of artistic processes, techniques and creative careers.
Careers
Art develops creativity, communication, problem-solving and critical thinking skills that are valued across many industries. Former students have pursued careers in:
Fine Art and Creative Industries
Highlights
The department has its own photography studio, darkroom facilities and specialist equipment.
Students work with an exceptional range of media, from oil paint and watercolour to photography, textiles and sculpture.
Miss Joe Thackray studied Fine Art Textiles at Loughborough University before completing her PGCE in Art at the University of Sussex. After leading a large art department in West Sussex for fifteen years, she joined Mayfield as Head of Art in 2006.
Passionate about art education and the transformative power of creativity, Miss Thackray enjoys helping students develop confidence in their artistic voice. She continues to expand her own practice through oil painting, mixed media and textile work, bringing fresh inspiration and expertise to the department.
Miss Hannah Oliver joined Mayfield in 2014 and teaches Photography and Digital Manipulation within the GCSE and A Level Art curriculum. A Fine Art Photography graduate from the University of Kent, she enjoys helping students develop creative ideas through photography, digital processes and design.

pageCache.pageTitle: Business Studies - Catholic Girls School | Mayfield School
pageCache.text:
Business Studies
Understanding How Organisations Succeed
Business is one of the most dynamic and relevant subjects students can study. It explores how organisations operate, compete and grow, while examining the decisions that shape successful companies. Using real-world examples and current business issues, students develop analytical thinking, commercial awareness and problem-solving skills that prepare them for university and beyond.
The Curriculum
Business is offered at A Level and provides students with a broad understanding of how organisations are managed and how strategic decisions are made. Students study:
Operations Management
Real-world case studies are used throughout the course to bring theory to life and help students understand how businesses respond to challenges and opportunities. Taught in small groups by specialist teachers, students are encouraged to think independently, challenge ideas and develop a critical understanding of the business world.
Three Mayfield students reached the final of the Hustle Lab's International AI Business Challenge
Beyond the Classroom
Students are encouraged to apply their learning beyond lessons through enterprise activities, competitions and engagement with current business issues. These opportunities help students develop confidence, teamwork and entrepreneurial thinking.
Degree Courses
Business provides an excellent foundation for a wide range of university courses, including:
International Business
Accounting and Finance
Highlights
A team of three Mayfield students reached the final of the Hustle Lab's International AI Business Challenge.
Business is taught in small groups within the Sixth Form Centre, enabling lively discussion and personalised support.
Careers
Former students have gone on to careers in:
Business and Management
Retail and Brand Management
Mrs Ania Cox holds a degree in Business Economics and Finance from Loughborough University and has more than twenty years' teaching experience. As a Senior Examiner for AQA, she brings extensive subject expertise to the classroom and is passionate about helping students understand the fast-moving world of business and develop the confidence to apply their knowledge beyond school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Ceramics - Girls Independent School | Mayfield School
pageCache.text:
Ceramics
Where creativity takes shape
Ceramics offers students a unique opportunity to explore creativity through making. Working with clay develops imagination, technical skill and confidence, while encouraging students to think critically, solve problems and bring their ideas to life.
At Mayfield, students learn in a supportive and stimulating environment where experimentation, individuality and craftsmanship are celebrated.
Mayfield's Pottery Studio is considered one of the finest school ceramics facilities in Europe
The Curriculum
Ceramics combines creative expression with technical understanding, allowing students to develop both practical and analytical skills. Students learn to:
Design and create original ceramic pieces
Explore a range of hand-building and decorative techniques
Develop analytical and aesthetic judgement
Draw inspiration from historical and contemporary ceramic artists
Understand the cultural significance of ceramics across different societies
The subject appeals to both artistic and scientifically minded students, combining creativity with problem-solving and design thinking.
Teaching takes place in Mayfield's dedicated Pottery Studio, widely regarded as one of the finest school ceramics facilities in Europe, providing extensive opportunities for research, experimentation and practical work.
Beyond the Classroom
Ceramics is enriched through opportunities to engage with professional artists and the wider creative community.
Students benefit from:
Working alongside our Artist in Residence
Demonstrations and workshops with visiting ceramicists
Museum and gallery visits
Opportunities to learn from professional practitioners
Each year, the department hosts its annual Potter's Day, welcoming a ceramic artist of national or international standing to deliver lectures, demonstrations and practical workshops.
Degree Courses
Ceramics complements a wide range of university pathways by developing creativity, design thinking and problem-solving skills. Recent students have progressed to courses including:
Ceramics and Fine Art
Design-related disciplines
Highlights
Every year, students meet and learn from a nationally or internationally recognised ceramic artist at the department's annual Potter's Day.
Over the last six years, A Level Ceramics students have achieved 32 A* grades and 14 A grades.
Trips
Students regularly visit museums and galleries to gain inspiration and experience artworks firsthand, supporting both practical work and wider cultural understanding.
Careers
Students have gone on to careers and further study in areas including:
Ceramics and Fine Art
Ms Yolanda McFadyean discovered her passion for ceramics while at school in East Sussex before studying Ceramics at Camberwell School of Art in London. A practising ceramic artist, she has exhibited in galleries across the South East and London, with her work featured in Ceramics Review.
Having joined Mayfield in 2002, Ms McFadyean has inspired generations of students through her enthusiasm for the subject and was appointed Head of Ceramics in 2026. She is passionate about helping students discover the creative possibilities of clay and develop confidence through making.

pageCache.pageTitle: Classics - All Girl Boarding & Day School | Mayfield School
pageCache.text:
Classics
Classics is the study of the languages, culture, history and thought of the civilisations of Ancient Greece and Rome. As such, it is one of the most interdisciplinary of subjects, making it constantly fresh and challenging, and encouraging mental versatility. Girls develop their essay writing skills and analytical skills, looking at works of art, historical documents and texts written in their original languages. Reading of the world’s greatest literature is also an essential part of the course.
At A Level and at GCSE, enthusiastic and experienced teachers, with excellent subject knowledge, teach the girls. The Classics Department is based in three classrooms and girls have the opportunity to visit museums, lectures and take part in trips to both Greece and Rome, over the course of their studies. Girls who take the subject at A Level have progressed to Oxbridge (Classics) and to Russell Group Universities, particularly Warwick. Undergraduate courses can be pure Classics or a combination of Classics with modern languages or English. The Classics Department prides itself on the number of opportunities it offers beyond the classroom. In the Lower School, trips are arranged to St Albans, Butser Celtic Farm and Fishbourne Palace. From Year 10 there are biennial trips to Rome and Pompeii, or Athens and Delphi. There are also regular competitions displayed on the Classics Board and a variety of clubs, ranging from Latin Scholars to Ancient Crafts, with Greek language classes pre-GCSE.

pageCache.pageTitle: Economics - Girls Independent School | Mayfield School
pageCache.text:
Economics
The study of Economics is all about the allocation of scarce resources, or who gets what, why, where and how. Economics gives us an understanding of how and why we place values on the things in our lives. It can explain why global financial crises arise, why a cup of coffee costs £2.20 in Starbucks but only 85p in the local café, and why footballers get paid $$$ but nurses only $. Economics will give you the tools to understand the world around us, from the actions of governments, to the decisions of people in the biscuit aisle in Sainsbury's.
Economics is a popular Sixth Form choice. Globalisation, employment, inflation, consumption, growth and financial planning are issues which affect all of us. The subject helps girls to develop a wide range of skills - knowledge, debate, analysis, synthesis, evaluation and organisation. Economics is taught in small groups by a specialist teacher in a dedicated room in the Sixth Form Centre. It can be chosen in conjunction with any other combination of subjects, but links particularly well with Geography, Politics and Maths. Many girls go on to study Economics related degrees, such as straight Economics, Banking and Finance, Econometrics, PPE, Economics and Management and International Relations, at a wide range of universities. All girls take part in a student investor share trading challenge, where teams of four invest a virtual £100,000 in a share portfolio with a chance of winning cash prizes and a trip to New York. Girls also enter the annual RES Economics essay competition as well as various other essay competitions throughout their period of study.
Ania Cox is the Head of Economics and Business Studies. She has a Business Economics and Finance degree from Loughborough University and has been a teacher for over 15 years. She is also a Senior Examiner for AQA.

Inspection Reports
We are delighted to share our most recent ISI report, following an inspection in March 2026.
The ISI regularly inspects independent schools to ensure the highest standards are upheld. Schools are evaluated against five key areas, with outcomes recorded as either met or not met. The inspection confirmed that Mayfield School met all standards.
We are especially proud that our co-curricular and enrichment programme, in which every pupil participates, was identified as a significant strength of the school. This is a rare recognition, achieved by fewer than 10% of inspected schools nationally.
“The extensive and highly effective co-curricular activity and enrichment programme, in which all pupils take part, is a significant strength of the school. The programme is explicitly designed to cultivate extra skills and qualities to complement the taught curriculum.”
“The programme cultivates essential skills and key personal qualities that equip pupils well for their future adult lives.”
The full report and a summary of key highlights are available below.
